title: Young Children Value the Lives of Animals More Than Adults Do

mock_data.title: Young Children Value the Lives of Animals More Than Adults Do
mock_data.passage:
A psychology news article about how children prioritize animal lives.

If you had to save the life of a person or an animal, which would you choose? Most adults say they would pick the person, but almost half of young children would prefer to save the animal, according to a study in Poland.

"The finding really surprised us," says Matti Wilks at the University of Edinburgh, UK.

Most adults view human life as especially precious. For example, a survey of millions of people in 233 countries, most of them in their 20s and 30s, found they largely agreed that self-driving cars should crash into dogs or cats instead of people if they had to choose.

However, growing evidence suggests many young children feel differently. Using a toy railway and Lego figures, Wilks and her colleagues presented 170 children aged 6 to 9 in an urban part of Poland with scenarios based on a thought experiment called the trolley problem.

The children had to decide whether to direct a runaway rail car down one of two tracks so that it crashed into a Lego person or a Lego animal – either a dog or chimpanzee. For comparison, the researchers repeated this with 178 Polish adults aged 18 to 50.

About 42 per cent of the children wanted to save the dog and make the rail car collide with the person, compared with just 17 per cent of adults. About 28 per cent of children also prioritised the chimpanzee over the person, compared with 11 per cent of adults.

Wilks and her colleagues have previously found that 28 per cent of children aged 5 to 9 in urban areas of New England in the US said they would save a dog over a person if they had to rescue one from a sinking ship, compared with 8 per cent of adults. About 18 per cent of children in that study also said they would save a pig over a person, compared with 3 per cent of adults.

"Children learn from their parents, teachers and others that it's really important to care for others, but it may be easier for them to learn this as a blanket rule that applies to both humans and animals," says Karri Neldner at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Germany. As a result, they don't show a strong preference for saving one over the other, she says.

"However, as they get older, they might pick up on cultural narratives that tell us it's really important to care for other people," says Neldner.

Her research suggests this shift starts by the age of 10. When she asked Australian children aged 4 to 10 to order pictures of people, animals, plants and objects according to how much they cared about them, the 4-year-olds tended to care more about dogs, cats and dolphins than about classmates, police officers and sick people, but this was reversed in the 10-year-olds.

The reason children value dogs so highly is probably due to familiarity, says Wilks. Her studies have found that children who spent more time with dogs were more likely to say they would save a dog over a person.
mock_data.passageB1:
Imagine you have to choose between saving a person or an animal. What would you do? Most adults say they would save the person. But a new study from Poland shows that many young children would rather save the animal.

Matti Wilks, a researcher from the UK, said that this finding was very surprising. Adults usually think that human life is more important than animal life. For example, a big survey asked many people what self-driving cars should do in an accident. Most people said the car should hit a dog or cat instead of a person.

But new evidence suggests that young children may think differently. Wilks and her team used a toy train and Lego figures to ask 170 children (aged 6 to 9) what they would do in a difficult situation. This situation is called the “trolley problem.”

The children had to decide if they would make the train go down a track and hit a Lego person or a Lego animal (a dog or a chimpanzee). The researchers also asked 178 adults (aged 18 to 50) the same question, to compare their answers.

About 42% of the children said they would save the dog and let the train hit the person. Only 17% of the adults said the same thing. Also, about 28% of the children said they would save the chimpanzee over the person. Only 11% of the adults agreed with them.

Wilks and her team had also done a similar study in the US. They found that 28% of children (aged 5 to 9) said they would save a dog instead of a person from a sinking ship. Only 8% of adults said the same. In that study, 18% of children said they would save a pig over a person, compared to 3% of adults.

Karri Neldner, a researcher from Germany, says that children learn from their parents and teachers to care about others. It might be easier for them to think that this rule applies to both humans and animals. So, they don't have a strong preference for saving one over the other.

Neldner also says that as children get older, they might start to understand that it's more important to care for other people. Her research shows that this change starts around the age of 10. She asked children (aged 4 to 10) to put pictures of people, animals, plants, and objects in order of how much they cared about them.

The 4-year-olds cared more about dogs, cats, and dolphins than about their classmates, police officers, and sick people. But the 10-year-olds cared more about the people. The reason children value dogs so much might be because they are more familiar with them, says Wilks. Her studies show that children who spend more time with dogs are more likely to say they would save a dog over a person.

In conclusion, this research shows that young children often prioritize animal lives over human lives, which is different from most adults. This may be because children learn to care for all living things, and it is only later that they learn to value human life more.
mock_data.passageB2:
Imagine you had to make a difficult choice: save a person's life or an animal's. Which would you choose? While most adults would likely prioritise saving the human, a recent study conducted in Poland suggests that a surprisingly large number of young children would opt to save the animal instead.

“The results were quite unexpected,” explains Dr. Matti Wilks from the University of Edinburgh, one of the researchers involved in the study. This finding challenges the common assumption that humans are inherently valued above all other living creatures.

Adults generally consider human life to be exceptionally valuable, often demonstrating this belief in various ways. For example, a large-scale survey involving millions of people from over 200 countries revealed a widespread agreement that self-driving cars, in unavoidable accident scenarios, should be programmed to minimise harm to humans, even if it means colliding with animals like dogs or cats.

However, a growing body of evidence indicates that young children may hold different values. To investigate this further, Dr. Wilks and her team used a creative method involving a toy railway and Lego figures to present 170 children, aged 6 to 9, with a variation of the classic “trolley problem.” This was done in an urban area of Poland.

The children were presented with a scenario where a runaway train car was headed towards a Lego person on one track and a Lego animal (either a dog or a chimpanzee) on another. They had to decide which track to direct the train towards. For comparison, the researchers replicated the experiment with 178 Polish adults aged 18 to 50.

The results showed a significant difference between the two groups. Approximately 42% of the children chose to save the dog, effectively sacrificing the Lego person, compared to only 17% of the adults. Similarly, around 28% of the children prioritised saving the chimpanzee over the person, whereas only 11% of the adults did so.

Dr. Wilks and her colleagues had previously observed a similar trend in the United States. In a study conducted in urban New England, they found that 28% of children aged 5 to 9 would save a dog over a person in a hypothetical sinking ship scenario, compared to just 8% of adults. Furthermore, 18% of the children indicated they would save a pig over a person, while only 3% of the adults agreed.

Karri Neldner, a researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, suggests that children's initial inclination to value animals equally to humans may stem from early learning experiences. “Children are taught to care for others, and they may initially interpret this as a universal principle applicable to both humans and animals,” she explains. This means they don't initially distinguish between the value of a human and animal life.

“However, as children mature, they are likely to internalise societal norms that emphasise the importance of caring for other people,” Neldner adds. This shift in perspective often begins around the age of 10, according to her research.

In her study, Australian children aged 4 to 10 were asked to rank pictures of people, animals, plants, and objects based on how much they cared about them. The 4-year-olds tended to place a higher value on dogs, cats, and dolphins than on classmates, police officers, and sick people. However, this pattern was reversed in the 10-year-olds, indicating a change in their value system.

Dr. Wilks believes that children's strong affection for dogs is likely due to familiarity. Her research has shown that children who spend more time with dogs are more likely to choose to save a dog over a person in hypothetical scenarios. This highlights the role of personal experience in shaping moral values.
mock_data.passageC1:
A fascinating divergence in moral priorities emerges when examining how different age groups value life: while adults tend to prioritise human life above all else, a recent study conducted in Poland suggests that young children may, in fact, ascribe greater importance to the lives of animals. This counter-intuitive finding, which challenges conventional assumptions about our inherent biases, indicates a potentially profound difference in how children and adults perceive the intrinsic worth of different species.

The study, spearheaded by Matti Wilks at the University of Edinburgh, throws into sharp relief the adult tendency to view human life as uniquely sacrosanct. For instance, a large-scale survey encompassing millions of individuals across 233 countries, predominantly those in their 20s and 30s, revealed a broad consensus that autonomous vehicles should, in a life-or-death scenario, be programmed to sacrifice animals, such as dogs or cats, rather than human beings. This utilitarian calculation, prioritising the preservation of human life, appears to be a deeply ingrained principle for most adults.

However, an accumulation of evidence suggests that this anthropocentric perspective is not universally shared, particularly among young children. Wilks and her team employed a modified version of the classic trolley problem, utilising a toy railway and Lego figures, to present 170 children aged 6 to 9, residing in an urban area of Poland, with a series of moral dilemmas. The children were tasked with deciding whether to redirect a runaway rail car towards a Lego person or a Lego animal – specifically, either a dog or a chimpanzee. A control group of 178 Polish adults, aged 18 to 50, was subjected to the same experimental conditions for comparative purposes.

The results were striking: approximately 42 per cent of the children expressed a preference for saving the dog, thereby consigning the Lego person to its fate. This figure stands in stark contrast to the mere 17 per cent of adults who favoured the animal's survival. A similar pattern emerged with the chimpanzee scenario, with 28 per cent of children prioritising the ape over the person, compared to a mere 11 per cent of the adult participants. These findings beg the question: what accounts for this developmental shift in moral reasoning?

This pattern is not isolated to the Polish study. Wilks and her colleagues had previously observed a similar phenomenon in the United States. Their research revealed that 28 per cent of children aged 5 to 9, living in urban areas of New England, indicated they would rescue a dog over a person from a sinking ship, whereas only 8 per cent of adults shared this sentiment. Furthermore, approximately 18 per cent of children in that study stated they would save a pig over a person, compared to a negligible 3 per cent of adults. These consistent findings underscore the developmental trajectory of moral values.

Karri Neldner at the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology posits that children's initial moral compass may be less discriminatory. “Children learn from their parents, teachers and others that it's really important to care for others, but it may be easier for them to learn this as a blanket rule that applies to both humans and animals,” she explains. Consequently, they may not initially exhibit a strong preference for saving one over the other. However, Neldner suggests that, as children mature, they become increasingly attuned to cultural narratives that emphasise the paramount importance of human life, leading to a recalibration of their moral priorities.

Neldner’s research indicates that this shift typically begins around the age of 10. Her study, which involved asking Australian children aged 4 to 10 to rank pictures of people, animals, plants, and objects according to their perceived importance, revealed that younger children (4-year-olds) tended to value dogs, cats, and dolphins more highly than classmates, police officers, and sick individuals. However, this trend was reversed in the 10-year-olds, suggesting a critical juncture in the development of anthropocentric biases. The underlying reasons behind this transformation remain a subject of ongoing investigation.

Wilks suggests that familiarity may play a pivotal role, particularly in the case of dogs. Her research has demonstrated a correlation between the amount of time children spend with dogs and their likelihood of prioritising a dog's life over a human's. This suggests that personal experience and emotional bonds can significantly exert influence on moral decision-making, particularly in the formative years. It remains to be seen what the far-reaching implications of these findings are for our understanding of moral development and the societal values we instill in future generations.

mock_data.translation:
Bolalarning hayvonlar hayotini qanday ustuvor qo'yishi haqida psixologiya yangiliklari maqolasi.

Agar siz odam yoki hayvonning hayotini saqlab qolishingiz kerak bo'lsa, qaysi birini tanlagan bo'lardingiz? Ko'pchilik kattalari odamni tanlashini aytishadi, lekin Polshadagi tadqiqotga ko'ra, yosh bolalarning deyarli yarmi hayvonni qutqarishni afzal ko'radi.

"Topilma bizni haqiqatan ham hayratda qoldirdi," deydi Buyuk Britaniya, Edinburg universitetidan Matti Uilks.

Ko'pchilik kattalari inson hayotini ayniqsa qimmatli deb hisoblaydi. Masalan, 233 mamlakatda millionlab odamlar orasida o'tkazilgan so'rovnomada, ularning aksariyati 20 va 30 yoshlarda bo'lib, ular o'z-o'zidan harakatlanuvchi mashinalar tanlash kerak bo'lsa, odamlar o'rniga it yoki mushuklarga urilishi kerakligiga asosan rozi bo'lgan.

Biroq, ko'payib borayotgan dalillar ko'plab yosh bolalar boshqacha his qilishini ko'rsatadi. O'yinchoq temir yo'l va Lego figuralaridan foydalanib, Uilks va uning hamkasblari Polshaning shahar qismida 6 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha bo'lgan 170 nafar bolaga tramvay muammosi deb ataladigan fikrlash tajribasiga asoslangan stsenariylarni taqdim etishdi.

Bolalar boshqarilmaydigan temir yo'l vagonini ikki yo'ldan biriga yo'naltirish kerakmi, deb qaror qilishlari kerak edi, shunda u Lego odamga yoki Lego hayvonga - itga yoki shimpanzega uriladi. Taqqoslash uchun tadqiqotchilar buni 18 yoshdan 50 yoshgacha bo'lgan 178 nafar Polsha kattalari bilan takrorladilar.

Bolalarning taxminan 42 foizi itni saqlab qolishni va poyezd vagonini odamga urilishini xohladi, holbuki kattalarning atigi 17 foizi shunday dedi. Bolalarning taxminan 28 foizi ham shimpanzeni odamdan ustun qo'ydi, holbuki kattalarning 11 foizi shunday qildi.

Uilks va uning hamkasblari ilgari AQShning Yangi Angliya shahar hududlarida 5 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha bo'lgan bolalarning 28 foizi cho'kayotgan kemadan birini qutqarish kerak bo'lsa, odamdan ko'ra itni qutqarishini aytganini aniqlagan, holbuki kattalarning 8 foizi shunday degan. O'sha tadqiqotda bolalarning taxminan 18 foizi ham odam o'rniga cho'chqani qutqarishini aytgan, kattalarning 3 foiziga nisbatan.

"Bolalar ota-onalari, o'qituvchilari va boshqalardan boshqalarga g'amxo'rlik qilish juda muhimligini o'rganadilar, lekin ular uchun buni ham odamlarga, ham hayvonlarga tegishli bo'lgan umumiy qoida sifatida o'rganish osonroq bo'lishi mumkin," deydi Germaniyaning Evolyutsion Antropologiya Max Plank Institutidan Karri Neldner. Natijada, ular birini boshqasidan qutqarishga kuchli afzallik ko'rsatmaydi, deydi u.

"Biroq, ular kattaroq bo'lganlarida, boshqa odamlarga g'amxo'rlik qilish juda muhim ekanligini aytadigan madaniy hikoyalarni o'zlashtirishlari mumkin," deydi Neldner.

Uning tadqiqotlari bu o'zgarish 10 yoshga kelib boshlanishini ko'rsatadi. U Avstraliya bolalaridan 4 yoshdan 10 yoshgacha odamlar, hayvonlar, o'simliklar va buyumlar rasmlarini qanchalik g'amxo'rlik qilishlariga qarab tartibga solishni so'raganida, 4 yoshlilar sinfdoshlar, politsiyachilar va kasal odamlarga qaraganda itlar, mushuklar va delfinlarga ko'proq g'amxo'rlik qilishga moyil bo'lgan, lekin bu 10 yoshlilarda aksincha edi.

Bolalar itlarni shunchalik yuqori baholashlarining sababi, ehtimol, tanishlik tufaylidir, deydi Uilks. Uning tadqiqotlari shuni ko'rsatdiki, itlar bilan ko'proq vaqt o'tkazgan bolalar odamdan ko'ra itni qutqarishini aytishlari ehtimoli ko'proq edi.

mock_data.translationB1:
Tasavvur qiling, siz odamni qutqarish yoki hayvonni qutqarish o'rtasida tanlov qilishga majbursiz. Nima qilardingiz? Ko'pchilik kattalar odamni qutqarishini aytadi. Ammo Polshadan olingan yangi tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, ko'plab yosh bolalar hayvonni qutqarishni afzal ko'rishadi.

Buyuk Britaniyalik tadqiqotchi Matti Wilksning aytishicha, bu natija juda hayratlanarli. Kattalar odatda inson hayoti hayvon hayotidan muhimroq deb hisoblashadi. Masalan, katta so'rov ko'plab odamlardan o'z-o'zidan harakatlanuvchi mashinalar baxtsiz hodisada nima qilishi kerakligini so'radi. Ko'pchilik mashina odam o'rniga it yoki mushukni urishi kerakligini aytdi.

Ammo yangi dalillar shuni ko'rsatadiki, yosh bolalar boshqacha fikrlashi mumkin. Wilks va uning jamoasi 170 nafar boladan (6 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha) qiyin vaziyatda nima qilishlarini so'rash uchun o'yinchoq poyezd va Lego figuralaridan foydalanishdi. Bu vaziyat "trolley muammosi" deb ataladi.

Bolalar poyezdni relsdan pastga tushirib, Lego odami yoki Lego hayvonini (it yoki shimpanze) urishga qaror qilishlari kerak edi. Tadqiqotchilar, shuningdek, 178 nafar kattalarga (18 yoshdan 50 yoshgacha) ularning javoblarini taqqoslash uchun xuddi shu savolni berishdi.

Bolalarning taxminan 42 foizi itni qutqarishini va poyezd odamni urishiga yo'l qo'yishini aytdi. Kattalarning atigi 17 foizi xuddi shunday dedi. Shuningdek, bolalarning taxminan 28 foizi odamdan ko'ra shimpanzeni qutqarishini aytdi. Kattalarning atigi 11 foizi ularga qo'shildi.

Wilks va uning jamoasi AQShda ham shunga o'xshash tadqiqot o'tkazishdi. Ular 5 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha bo'lgan bolalarning 28 foizi cho'kayotgan kemadan odam o'rniga itni qutqarishini aytishgan. Kattalarning atigi 8 foizi xuddi shunday dedi. Ushbu tadqiqotda bolalarning 18 foizi odamdan ko'ra cho'chqani qutqarishini aytishdi, taqqoslaganda kattalarning 3 foizi.

Germaniyalik tadqiqotchi Karri Neldnerning aytishicha, bolalar ota-onalari va o'qituvchilaridan boshqalarga g'amxo'rlik qilishni o'rganadilar. Ularga bu qoida ham odamlarga, ham hayvonlarga tegishli ekanligini o'ylash osonroq bo'lishi mumkin. Shunday qilib, ularning birini ikkinchisidan ko'ra qutqarishga kuchli afzalligi yo'q.

Neldnerning ta'kidlashicha, bolalar ulg'aygan sari, boshqa odamlarga g'amxo'rlik qilish muhimroq ekanligini tushunishlari mumkin. Uning tadqiqotlari shuni ko'rsatadiki, bu o'zgarish taxminan 10 yoshdan boshlanadi. U bolalardan (4 yoshdan 10 yoshgacha) odamlarning, hayvonlarning, o'simliklarning va narsalarning rasmlarini ularga qanchalik g'amxo'rlik qilish tartibida joylashtirishni so'radi.

4 yoshli bolalar sinfdoshlari, politsiyachilar va kasal odamlarga qaraganda itlar, mushuklar va delfinlarga ko'proq g'amxo'rlik qilishdi. Ammo 10 yoshli bolalar odamlarga ko'proq g'amxo'rlik qilishdi. Bolalarning itlarni bunchalik qadrlashi sababi ularning ular bilan yaxshiroq tanishligi bo'lishi mumkin, deydi Wilks. Uning tadqiqotlari shuni ko'rsatadiki, itlar bilan ko'proq vaqt o'tkazadigan bolalar odamdan ko'ra itni qutqarishini aytish ehtimoli ko'proq.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, bu tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, yosh bolalar ko'pincha hayvonlar hayotini inson hayotidan ustun qo'yishadi, bu ko'pchilik kattalardan farq qiladi. Buning sababi shundaki, bolalar barcha tirik mavjudotlarga g'amxo'rlik qilishni o'rganadilar va faqat keyinroq inson hayotini qadrlashni o'rganadilar.
mock_data.translationB2:
Tasavvur qiling, siz qiyin tanlov oldidasiz: insonning hayotini saqlab qolish yoki hayvonning. Qaysi birini tanlagan bo'lardingiz? Aksariyat kattalar insonni qutqarishni ustuvor bilishsa-da, Polshada o'tkazilgan so'nggi tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, hayratlanarli darajada ko'p sonli yosh bolalar buning o'rniga hayvonni qutqarishni tanlaydi.

“Natijalar juda ham kutilmagan bo'ldi”, deb tushuntiradi Edinburg universitetidan doktor Matti Wilks, tadqiqotda ishtirok etgan tadqiqotchilardan biri. Bu topilma insonlar boshqa barcha tirik mavjudotlardan ustun turadi, degan keng tarqalgan taxminga qarshi chiqadi.

Kattalar, odatda, inson hayotini juda qadrlashadi va bu e'tiqodni turli yo'llar bilan namoyon etishadi. Misol uchun, 200 dan ortiq mamlakatdan millionlab odamlarni qamrab olgan keng ko'lamli so'rov shuni ko'rsatdiki, avtonom avtomobillar, muqarrar baxtsiz hodisa stsenariylarida, it yoki mushuk kabi hayvonlar bilan to'qnashuvga olib kelishi mumkin bo'lsa ham, insonlarga zararni kamaytirish uchun dasturlashtirilishi kerak degan keng tarqalgan kelishuv mavjud.

Biroq, ortib borayotgan dalillar shuni ko'rsatadiki, yosh bolalar boshqacha qadriyatlarga ega bo'lishi mumkin. Buni yanada o'rganish uchun doktor Wilks va uning jamoasi 6 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha bo'lgan 170 nafar bolaga klassik "trolley muammosi"ning o'zgartirilgan versiyasini taqdim etish uchun o'yinchoq temir yo'l va Lego figuralari yordamida ijodiy usuldan foydalanishdi. Bu Polshaning shahar hududida amalga oshirildi.

Bolalarga bir yo'lda Lego odamga, ikkinchi yo'lda esa Lego hayvoniga (it yoki shimpanze) qarab ketayotgan boshqaruvsiz vagoncha ssenariysi taqdim etildi. Ular qaysi yo'nalishga vagonchani yo'naltirishni hal qilishlari kerak edi. Taqqoslash uchun tadqiqotchilar 18 yoshdan 50 yoshgacha bo'lgan 178 nafar polshalik kattalar bilan tajribani takrorlashdi.

Natijalar ikki guruh o'rtasida sezilarli farq borligini ko'rsatdi. Bolalarning taxminan 42 foizi itni qutqarishni tanladi va amalda Lego odamini qurbon qildi, kattalarning atigi 17 foizi shunday qildi. Xuddi shunday, bolalarning taxminan 28 foizi shimpanzeni odamdan ustun qo'ydi, kattalarning esa atigi 11 foizi shunday qildi.

Doktor Wilks va uning hamkasblari avvalroq Qo'shma Shtatlarda shunga o'xshash tendentsiyani kuzatgan edilar. Yangi Angliyaning shahar hududida o'tkazilgan tadqiqotda ular 5 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha bo'lgan bolalarning 28 foizi gipotetik cho'kayotgan kemada itni odamdan ustun qo'yishini aniqladilar, kattalarning atigi 8 foizi shunday qilar edi. Bundan tashqari, bolalarning 18 foizi cho'chqani odamdan ustun qo'yishlarini ko'rsatdilar, kattalarning esa atigi 3 foizi rozi bo'lishdi.

Maks Plank Evolyutsion Antropologiya Institutining tadqiqotchisi Karri Neldnerning ta'kidlashicha, bolalarning hayvonlarni insonlar bilan teng qadrlashga bo'lgan dastlabki moyilligi erta o'rganish tajribalaridan kelib chiqishi mumkin. "Bolalarga boshqalarga g'amxo'rlik qilish o'rgatiladi va ular buni dastlab insonlar va hayvonlarga nisbatan qo'llaniladigan universal prinsip sifatida talqin qilishlari mumkin", deb tushuntiradi u. Bu shuni anglatadiki, ular dastlab inson va hayvon hayotining qiymatini farqlamaydilar.

"Biroq, bolalar ulg'aygan sari, ular boshqa insonlarga g'amxo'rlik qilish muhimligini ta'kidlaydigan ijtimoiy normalarni ichki tushunishlari mumkin", deb qo'shimcha qiladi Neldner. Uning tadqiqotlariga ko'ra, bu nuqtai nazar o'zgarishi ko'pincha 10 yoshdan boshlanadi.

Uning tadqiqotida 4 yoshdan 10 yoshgacha bo'lgan avstraliyalik bolalardan odamlar, hayvonlar, o'simliklar va ob'ektlarning rasmlarini ularga qanchalik g'amxo'rlik qilishlariga qarab tartiblash so'raldi. 4 yoshli bolalar sinfdoshlari, politsiya xodimlari va kasal odamlarga qaraganda itlar, mushuklar va delfinlarga ko'proq ahamiyat berishga moyil edilar. Biroq, bu naqsh 10 yoshli bolalarda teskari bo'ldi, bu ularning qadriyatlar tizimidagi o'zgarishni ko'rsatadi.

Doktor Wilksning fikricha, bolalarning itlarga bo'lgan kuchli mehr-muhabbati, ehtimol, tanishlik bilan bog'liq. Uning tadqiqotlari shuni ko'rsatdiki, itlar bilan ko'proq vaqt o'tkazadigan bolalar gipotetik stsenariylarda itni odamdan ustun qo'yishni tanlash ehtimoli ko'proq. Bu axloqiy qadriyatlarni shakllantirishda shaxsiy tajribaning rolini ta'kidlaydi.
mock_data.translationC1:
Hayotni qadrlash boʻyicha turli yosh guruhlari oʻrtasidagi farqni oʻrganishda qiziqarli tafovutlar yuzaga keladi: kattalar inson hayotini hamma narsadan ustun qoʻyishga moyil boʻlsa, Polshada oʻtkazilgan yaqinda oʻtkazilgan tadqiqot shuni koʻrsatadiki, yosh bolalar, aslida, hayvonlarning hayotiga koʻproq ahamiyat berishlari mumkin. Bizning tabiiy xolisligimiz haqidagi odatiy taxminlarga zid boʻlgan bu kutilmagan topilma bolalar va kattalar turli xil turlarning oʻziga xos qadrini qanday qabul qilishida chuqur farq borligini koʻrsatadi.

Edinburg universitetidan Matti Wilks boshchiligidagi tadqiqot kattalarning inson hayotini oʻzgacha muqaddas deb bilish tendensiyasini yaqqol koʻrsatib beradi. Misol uchun, 233 ta mamlakatda millionlab odamlarni qamrab olgan keng koʻlamli soʻrov, asosan 20-30 yoshdagi odamlarda, avtonom transport vositalari hayot-mamot vaziyatida itlar yoki mushuklar kabi hayvonlarni qurbon qilish uchun dasturlashtirilishi kerak degan keng tarqalgan fikrni aniqladi, insonlar emas. Inson hayotini saqlab qolishni birinchi oʻringa qoʻyadigan bu utilitar hisob-kitob koʻpchilik kattalar uchun chuqur oʻrnashgan prinsip boʻlib tuyuladi.

Biroq, dalillarning toʻplanishi bu antroposentrik nuqtai nazar hamma tomonidan bir xilda qabul qilinmasligini, ayniqsa yosh bolalar orasida koʻrsatadi. Wilks va uning jamoasi klassik trolleybus muammosining oʻzgartirilgan versiyasidan foydalanib, oʻyinchoq temir yoʻli va Lego figuralaridan foydalanib, Polshaning shahar hududida yashovchi 6 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha boʻlgan 170 nafar bolaga bir qator axloqiy dilemmalarni taqdim etdi. Bolalarga qochib ketayotgan temir yoʻl vagonini Lego odamga yoki Lego hayvoniga – xususan, itga yoki shimpanzega yoʻnaltirish yoki yoʻnaltirmaslik haqida qaror qabul qilish vazifasi yuklatildi. Taqqoslash maqsadida 18 yoshdan 50 yoshgacha boʻlgan 178 nafar polshalik kattalardan iborat nazorat guruhi ham xuddi shu eksperimental sharoitlarga duch keldi.

Natijalar hayratlanarli edi: bolalarning taxminan 42 foizi itni saqlab qolishni afzal koʻrishdi va shu bilan Lego odamini oʻlimga mahkum qilishdi. Bu koʻrsatkich hayvonning omon qolishini yoqlagan kattalarning atigi 17 foiziga keskin zid keladi. Xuddi shunday holat shimpanze ssenariysi bilan ham yuzaga keldi, bolalarning 28 foizi maymunni odamdan ustun qoʻydi, kattalarning atigi 11 foizi esa shunday fikrda edi. Bu topilmalar savol tugʻdiradi: axloqiy mulohazadagi bu rivojlanish oʻzgarishiga nima sabab boʻladi?

Bu holat faqat Polsha tadqiqotida uchramaydi. Wilks va uning hamkasblari avvalroq Qoʻshma Shtatlarda ham shunga oʻxshash hodisani kuzatishgan. Ularning tadqiqotlari shuni koʻrsatdiki, Yangi Angliyaning shahar hududlarida yashovchi 5 yoshdan 9 yoshgacha boʻlgan bolalarning 28 foizi choʻkayotgan kemadan itni odamdan ustun koʻrishini aytgan, kattalarning atigi 8 foizi bu fikrga qoʻshilgan. Bundan tashqari, oʻsha tadqiqotda bolalarning taxminan 18 foizi choʻchqani odamdan ustun koʻrishini aytgan, kattalarning atigi 3 foizi esa shunday fikrda edi. Ushbu izchil topilmalar axloqiy qadriyatlarning rivojlanish yoʻlini taʼkidlaydi.

Maks Plank Evolyutsion Antropologiya Institutidan Karri Neldnerning taʼkidlashicha, bolalarning dastlabki axloqiy kompaslari kamroq kamsituvchi boʻlishi mumkin. "Bolalar ota-onalari, oʻqituvchilari va boshqalardan boshqalarga gʻamxoʻrlik qilish juda muhimligini oʻrganadilar, lekin ular buni ham odamlarga, ham hayvonlarga tegishli boʻlgan qoida sifatida oʻrganishlari osonroq boʻlishi mumkin", deydi u. Natijada, ular dastlab birini ikkinchisidan ustun qoʻyishga kuchli moyillik koʻrsatmasligi mumkin. Biroq, Neldnerning taʼkidlashicha, bolalar ulgʻaygan sayin, inson hayotining muhimligini taʼkidlaydigan madaniy rivoyatlarga tobora koʻproq eʼtibor qaratadilar, bu esa ularning axloqiy ustuvorliklarini qayta kalibrlashga olib keladi.

Neldnerning tadqiqotlari shuni koʻrsatadiki, bu oʻzgarish odatda 10 yosh atrofida boshlanadi. Uning 4 yoshdan 10 yoshgacha boʻlgan avstraliyalik bolalardan odamlar, hayvonlar, oʻsimliklar va narsalarning rasmlarini ularning qabul qilingan ahamiyatiga qarab tartiblashni soʻrashni oʻz ichiga olgan tadqiqoti shuni koʻrsatdiki, yosh bolalar (4 yoshlilar) itlar, mushuklar va delfinlarni sinfdoshlar, politsiyachilar va kasal odamlardan koʻra koʻproq qadrlashga moyil edilar. Biroq, bu tendentsiya 10 yoshlilarda teskari yoʻnalishda edi, bu antroposentrik xolisliklarning rivojlanishida muhim burilish nuqtasi ekanligini koʻrsatadi. Bu oʻzgarishning asosiy sabablari doimiy ravishda oʻrganilmoqda.

Wilksning taʼkidlashicha, tanishlik, ayniqsa itlar holatida, hal qiluvchi rol oʻynashi mumkin. Uning tadqiqotlari bolalarning itlar bilan qancha vaqt oʻtkazishi va ularning it hayotini inson hayotidan ustun qoʻyish ehtimoli oʻrtasida bogʻliqlik borligini koʻrsatdi. Bu shuni koʻrsatadiki, shaxsiy tajriba va hissiy bogʻlanishlar axloqiy qaror qabul qilishga, ayniqsa shakllanish yillarida sezilarli taʼsir koʻrsatishi mumkin. Ushbu topilmalarning axloqiy rivojlanish va kelajak avlodlarga singdiradigan ijtimoiy qadriyatlar haqidagi tushunchamiz uchun keng koʻlamli oqibatlari qanday boʻlishini koʻrish kerak.
